title: A 66 MB stand-in caught a bug that sat in main for two months
friendlyTitle: A tiny test model caught a bug that hid for two months
summary: Hugging Face proposes Model Integration Contracts: a shrunk copy of a real model, a short usage example, and human-reviewed expected outputs, run on CPU. A 66 MB UMT5 fixture flagged a 30 July change that let the decoder attend to future tokens. The bug stayed in Transformers main until 28 September. A plain forward pass would not have caught it.
friendlySummary: Hugging Face describes a way to test big AI models with a much smaller copy that still uses the real code path. One of these small copies caught a bug that let a model peek at the answer it was supposed to predict. The bug had already been in the main code for almost two months.
whyItMatters: If you depend on a model library, the useful test is the path users actually run, including the default attention code, not only whether the model loads. An agent can draft the contract. A person still has to approve the expected outputs.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Loading a model is not the same as checking that it behaves. A small, repeatable test can catch that kind of mistake before users do, but a person still needs to approve what 'correct' means.
